title: Control Framework for Access, Change, and Travel
author: Elena Morales
body:
Overview

This document defines a single, company-wide control framework that ties together three frequently cross-cutting operational domains: Access & Permissions, Change Management, and Travel & Expense approvals. The goal is to provide clear guardrails, SLAs, and templates so teams can operate quickly while preserving security, auditability, and cost controls.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors accessing Redwood systems or services.
- Covers requests and approvals for: role-based access, elevated privilege (IAM/SSH/KMS), infrastructure and application changes, vendor travel and expense approvals, and procurement-related approvals tied to access or travel.

Principles
1. Least privilege by default: new accounts receive no elevated roles; request only the roles required for the task.
2. Separation of duties: approval and implementation should be distinct where practical.
3. Time-bounded elevation: temporary access should have an expiry date and automated revocation.
4. Evidence-first changes: every non-trivial change must include a rollback plan and test criteria.
5. Auditability: all approvals and major events stored in the central audit log for at least 3 years.

Ownership and Roles
- People Ops (policy owner): policy lifecycle, role taxonomy updates, travel policy exceptions. Owner: Elena Morales (people-ops@redwood.com)
- Security (approver for privileged access): approves vault/KMS/HSM escalations and vendor onboarding for secure environments. Contact: Samir Patel (security@redwood.com)
- Eng Platform (change steward): approves scheduled maintenance windows and high-risk infra changes. Contact: Jia Li (eng-platform@redwood.com)
- Finance (travel & procurement gates): approves travel budgets, high-value vendor spend, and reconciliations. Contact: Liam O'Connor (finance@redwood.com)

Key SLAs and Thresholds
- Standard access request: target approval time 72 hours.
- Urgent access request: target approval time 24 hours (must be tagged URGENT with justification and incident link).
- Vendor onboarding (access + contract > $50k): 10 business days end-to-end.
- Infrastructure change review (risk score >= 7): review decision within 5 business days and scheduled within next maintenance window.
- Travel expense pre-approval: must be submitted at least 7 business days before travel for non-local travel.

Access & Permissions (Process)
1) Requesting Access
   - Use the Access Request template in the Templates section below. Minimal required fields: requester, target resource, requested roles, business justification, expiry date, and reviewer (team lead).
   - All requests must be created via the central Requests tracker (link: /tools/access-requests). Requests initiated via email are not accepted unless tagged as exception in the request tracker.

2) Approval Matrix
   - Up to team-level roles: team lead approves.
   - Cross-team or org-level roles (roles granting >1 team visibility): Security + Team Lead.
   - Privileged secrets access (KMS/HSM/production DB credentials): Security + Eng Platform.
   - Vendor engineers: People Ops + Security + Contracting.

3) Time-bounded Elevation
   - Temporary roles must include expiry <= 14 days unless extended with documented justification. Automatic revocation is enforced via the identity system.

4) Revocation and Certification
   - Quarterly automated certification: team leads receive certification lists and must confirm or remove access within 10 business days.

Change Management (Process)
- Risk scoring: Changes are classified into Low, Medium, High based on impact, blast radius, and rollback complexity. The change template includes the risk score calculation (see template). High risk requires: pre-change runbook, rollback procedure, test plan, and a scheduled maintenance window.

Change stages (numbered):
1. Draft change request created with required fields: summary, owner, risk score, rollback plan, test verification steps, monitoring checklist, and backout ETA.
2. Peer review by the owning team and automated linting for infra-as-code (IaC) diffs.
3. Approval routing based on risk: team lead -> Eng Platform -> Security (if high).
4. Scheduling in maintenance window (typical windows: Tue 02:00-05:00 PT, Thu 01:00-04:00 PT); emergency patches handled via Emergency Change flow below.
5. Post-change verification and completion record stored in change log.

Emergency Change Flow
- Trigger: active incident or critical vulnerability.
- Approvals: on-call owner + Eng Platform + Security (can be asynchronous with post-hoc review).
- Must be followed by a formal change request in the backlog within 48 hours.

Data Management Requirements
- Data classification categories: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated. All systems must label data at source.
- Access to Confidential & Regulated data requires: approved access request, signed DPA (if external), and periodic review every 90 days.
- Retention & deletion: follow the Data Retention Schedule (link: /policies/data-retention). Requests for deletion must route through Data Governance.

Procurement and Expense Controls
- Procurement thresholds:
  * Up to $5k: team lead approval.
  * $5k - $50k: Finance approval required.
  * > $50k: Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor.
- Travel pre-approval matrix:
  * Domestic, <$2k: manager approval.
  * International or >= $2k: manager + Finance approval.
  * Hotel upgrades, business class travel: require executive sponsor sign-off for non-exceptional cases.
- Corporate cards: issued by People Ops; single-transaction limits default to $2k; exceptions require Finance approval.

Vendor Management with Access Considerations
- Onboarding checklist (required): signed contract, SOC2/ISO attestation as applicable, access scope spreadsheet, technical contact, and an exit plan.
- Vendor engineer access: limited to vendor-managed accounts where possible; if vendor needs Redwood-managed accounts, issue time-bound accounts with MFA and audit logging.
- Vendor travel: any vendor on Redwood premises must be pre-approved 72 hours in advance and have a sponsor.

Templates and Examples
- Access Request (YAML example):

  ---
  type: access_request
  requester: alice@redwood.com
  target: project-redwood/db-production
  roles:
    - read-only
  justification: 'Investigating query performance for ticket #1234'
  expiry: '2025-10-01'
  reviewer: team-lead@redwood.com
  ---

- Change Request (minimal fields):
  - summary
  - owner
  - risk_score (1-10)
  - rollback_plan
  - test_verification_steps

- Quick CLI snippet to create a request (internal tool):
  $ rw-ops request create --type access --resource "project-redwood/db" --roles "read-only" --expiry 14d --justification "support ticket 1234"

Audit & Evidence Requirements
- All approvals must be recorded in the central Requests tracker along with the approver's user id, timestamp, and rationale.
- For sensitive approvals (privileged access, high-risk changes, >$50k procurement), attach the signed approval PDF (e-sign) to the request record.
- Audit data retention: security logs 3 years, approval artifacts 7 years for contractual vendors.

Exception Handling and Escalation
- Exceptions to policy must be requested through the Exception Request form and include: scope, risk mitigation, compensating controls, owner, and expiration date.
- Exception approvals chain: People Ops -> Security -> Finance (if cost impacts) -> Executive sponsor (if > 90 days).

Enforcement and Violations
- Violations are categorized as Operational (process miss), Security (access misuse), and Financial (procurement misuse).
- Remediation steps depend on severity; examples include access revocation, re-training, reversal of spend, and disciplinary review per People Ops policy.

Operational Dashboards and Reporting
- Standard dashboards (links):
  * Access request backlog and mean time to approve
  * Pending change requests by risk bucket
  * Travel pre-approvals vs actual spend by org
  * Vendor access inventory and expiry distribution
- Monthly report owners: People Ops produces access & travel summary; Eng Platform produces change management metrics; Finance produces vendor spend rollup.

Onboarding and Training
- All new hires receive a 1-hour training on Access & Change controls during week-1 onboarding.
- Quarterly 30-minute refreshers are required for team leads and eng-oncall.

Appendix: Example Approval Matrix (ASCII table)

Role | Action Type | Approver(s) | SLA
---- | ----------- | ----------- | ----
Team-level role grant | Access | Team Lead | 72 hrs
Org-level role grant | Access | Team Lead + Security | 5 days
Privileged secret access | Access | Security + Eng Platform | 24 hrs (urgent)
Low risk infra change | Change | Team Lead | 3 days
High risk infra change | Change | Team Lead + Eng Platform + Security | 5 days
Travel (domestic < $2k) | Travel | Manager | 7 days before travel
Procurement > $50k | Spend | Finance + Legal + Exec | 10 business days
